artifact_or_text: Orphic Gold Funeral Lamellae (Hipponion, Petelia, Thurii, Pelinna)
theological_mapping: The soul possesses divine celestial heritage ('child of Earth and starry Heaven') trapped in a cycle of grief until purified by Dionysiac-Orphic ritual.
ritual_or_liturgical_use: Inscribed thin gold sheets folded and buried on the chest or mouth of deceased initiates as liturgical cue cards for answering Hades's guardians.
christological_comparison: Prefigures Christian baptismal confession and viaticum—giving the dying believer sacred words to cross from death into true memory and peace.

artifact_or_text: Derveni Papyrus Libations & The 87 Orphic Hymns
theological_mapping: Sacred verse acts as veiled cosmogony; priestly exegesis decodes mythic violence into divine cosmic intelligence (Zeus as Mind/Breath).
ritual_or_liturgical_use: Nocturnal mystery rites pairing honey-milk-water libations, unleavened ritual cakes with knobs, and burning specific aromatics per hymn.
christological_comparison: Resembles ancient Mediterranean liturgical incense usage and allegorical exegesis, though Orphic liturgy remains secretive and elitist rather than public kerygma.

artifact_or_text: Christus-Orpheus Frescoes (Catacombs of Domitilla, Callixtus, & Pietro e Marcellino)
theological_mapping: Christ is visually portrayed wearing Orpheus's Phrygian cap, holding the lyre among listening sheep, lions, and peacocks (symbols of resurrection).
ritual_or_liturgical_use: Painted directly on vault ceilings over arcosolia tombs where Roman Christians celebrated memorial meals and Eucharistic prayers for the dead.
christological_comparison: Positive typological bridge: Jesus fulfills what Orpheus promised—actually conquering Sheol/Hades and leading all creation back to peace.

artifact_or_text: Clement of Alexandria, Protrepticus (Exhortation to the Greeks), Ch. 1
theological_mapping: Contrasts the 'old deceitful song' of Thracian Orpheus (which tamed beasts only to bind humans to idols) with Christ the Logos, the 'New Song' (Psalm 96/98).
ritual_or_liturgical_use: Alexandrian baptismal & catechetical rhetoric preparing educated Greek converts to enter Christian worship.
christological_comparison: Polemical superiority: Orpheus only enchanted trees and rocks temporarily; Christ turns 'stony hearts' into living children of Abraham.

artifact_or_text: Eusebius of Caesarea, In Praise of Constantine (Tricennial Oration 14.5)
theological_mapping: Likens the Incarnate Word holding human nature as his 'lyre' to Orpheus, sounding divine harmony across a fractured empire.
ritual_or_liturgical_use: Imperial Christian liturgical-political panegyric celebrating cosmic peace under Christ's Cross.
christological_comparison: Moves from subterranean catacomb comfort to imperial theology: the Logos tunes all nations like strings of one cosmic instrument.

artifact_or_text: Boethius, Consolation of Philosophy III.m12 & Commentary Tradition
theological_mapping: Converts Orpheus's backward glance into Catholic moral-ascetic warning: turning back from God's light toward worldly attachments costs the soul its true beatitude.
ritual_or_liturgical_use: Studied across Benedictine monastic schools (Alcuin, Remigius of Auxerre) and cited in medieval Lenten/penitential reflection (echoing Luke 9:62: 'No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back...').
christological_comparison: Orpheus here represents the frail human intellect or pilgrim soul needing divine grace so it does not relapse at the threshold of heaven.

artifact_or_text: Ovide Moralisé (Book X) & Pierre Bersuire's Ovidius Moralizatus
theological_mapping: Applies the Catholic fourfold sense of Scripture to pagan myth: Orpheus = Christ descending into Limbo (Harrowing of Hell); Eurydice = Eve/Humanity; Viper = Satan; Lyre = the Cross / Harmony of the Two Testaments.
ritual_or_liturgical_use: Sourcebook for Catholic Holy Saturday & Eastertide preaching on Christ breaking the brass gates of Hell without looking back.
christological_comparison: Direct Harrowing of Hell typology: where Orpheus fails at the threshold and loses Eurydice, Christ succeeds completely and raises Adam and Eve forever.

artifact_or_text: Sir Orfeo (Middle English Breton Lai, Auchinleck Manuscript)
theological_mapping: Recasts Orpheus as a devout medieval Christian king who abdicates wealth, lives ten years in ascetic wilderness poverty, and trusts Providence rather than pride.
ritual_or_liturgical_use: Courtly and pious oral recitation teaching Christian kingship, marital fidelity, and mercy.
christological_comparison: Because Sir Orfeo acts with Christ-like self-emptying (kenosis) and patience, no backward-glance curse destroys his marriage—his queen returns alive.
